package_info.package_manager: standalone binary (Golang malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: Skuld is a purpose-built information stealer written in Golang, designed to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems. It targets credentials, browser data, Discord tokens, system information, clipboard contents, screenshots, and cryptocurrency wallet files. The malware employs multiple exfiltration channels (Discord webhooks, Gofile), anti-analysis techniques, and broad data collection, making it a clear and sophisticated threat.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Searches for and reads data from Discord application folders, browser credential stores (e.g., masterkey_db, login_db, download_db, history_db, card_db), and system folders.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and reads sensitive files from Discord, web browsers, and user/system directories, then prepares this data for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically accesses credential stores, browser databases, and Discord tokens without user consent, which is a hallmark of information-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications only access their own data or user-approved files, not credential stores or unrelated application data from other software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup tools may access browser data, but only with explicit user permission and clear user notification.
key_indicators: Automated access to browser credential stores (e.g., login_db, masterkey_db)
Enumeration and reading of Discord application data
Systematic search of user and system folders for sensitive files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Sends exfiltrated data to hardcoded Discord webhooks (e.g., https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...) and/or Gofile upload endpoints (https://api.gofile.io/getServer, gofile.io/uploadFile).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code transmits collected sensitive data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and/or Gofile servers via HTTPS POST requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to external web services, especially via hardcoded Discord webhooks and anonymous file sharing services, is a clear indicator of information stealer activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not send user credentials, tokens, or private data to external, hardcoded endpoints without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Bug reporting tools may send logs to a developer's server, but never credentials, tokens, or sensitive user data.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhooks for data exfiltration
Use of Gofile API endpoints for file upload
Presence of hardcoded external endpoints in binary

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Performs system checks to detect virtualization, sandboxes, or debugging environments (e.g., checking for known VM artifacts, registry keys, or process names).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects the environment for signs of virtualization or analysis tools, and may alter its behavior or terminate if detected.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-analysis and sandbox evasion techniques are commonly used by malware to avoid detection and hinder analysis by security researchers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely checks for virtualization or debuggers unless for licensing, support, or anti-piracy reasons, and never to evade detection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some commercial software may check for VMs to prevent piracy or for licensing enforcement, but not to evade security analysis.
key_indicators: VM/sandbox detection routines (e.g., checking for known VM files, registry keys, or process names)
Debugger evasion logic (e.g., process enumeration for analysis tools)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Captures clipboard data and/or takes screenshots of the user's desktop.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads clipboard contents and/or captures screenshots, then includes this data in the exfiltration payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing clipboard and screen data is a classic data theft technique, especially when combined with credential or session theft, and is not expected in normal user applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not capture clipboard or screen data without explicit user action and clear user notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support or screenshot tools may capture screens or clipboard data, but only with explicit user consent and visible prompts.
key_indicators: Screen capture routines in non-UI applications
Inclusion of clipboard/screenshot data in exfiltration payload

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Searches for and attempts to access cryptocurrency wallet files or modules (feature in development).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attempts to locate and access files or modules related to cryptocurrency wallets, potentially to steal wallet data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Targeting cryptocurrency wallets is a high-value theft behavior, and searching for wallet files is not expected in legitimate software unless it is a wallet manager.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not access or search for unrelated wallet files or modules without user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cryptocurrency management tools may access wallet files, but only with user consent and clear user interaction.
key_indicators: Automated search for wallet files or directories
Code modules referencing cryptocurrency assets or wallet formats

attack_chain.action: Malware is executed on the victim's system (user runs malicious EXE).
Performs anti-analysis checks to evade sandboxes and debuggers.
Enumerates and collects sensitive data: Discord tokens, browser credentials, system info, clipboard, screenshots, and (optionally) cryptocurrency wallets.
Exfiltrates collected data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and/or Gofile servers.

behavioral_signatures: Golang binary accessing browser credential stores and Discord application data
Network connections to Discord webhooks and Gofile API endpoints
Clipboard and screen capture activity by unknown or non-UI processes
Anti-analysis checks (VM, sandbox, debugger detection) in userland binaries
file_indicators: Access to browser database files such as masterkey_db, login_db, download_db, history_db, card_db
Searches for known cryptocurrency wallet file paths (e.g., wallet.dat, Electrum, Exodus, Atomic Wallet directories)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Outbound requests to https://api.gofile.io/getServer and gofile.io/uploadFile
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unknown Golang binaries accessing browser credential stores, Discord application data, or cryptocurrency wallet files. Flag processes making outbound HTTPS requests to Discord webhooks or Gofile endpoints, especially if preceded by credential, clipboard, or screenshot access. Detect anti-analysis routines by monitoring for system checks indicative of sandbox or debugger evasion. Correlate file access patterns with network exfiltration to identify information stealer activity. Use endpoint monitoring to alert on clipboard or screen capture activity by non-UI processes.
